one_line: Domain-specific WebMCP expertise for real Shopify stores.

leverage_rationale: Structured, schema-constrained domain advice materially improves reliability over a general agent reading a storefront, especially for sizing and medical-guardrail cases; shared data serves human and agent surfaces.
leverage_evidence: About text describes 15 tools per store, including five domain tools beyond Shopify defaults.
Decision tables live in JSON with tight schemas and additionalProperties:false.
Frame sheets show a real store/tool-oriented interface and results panel, though invocation details are not legible.
execution_rationale: The submission presents a coherent two-store implementation, shared knowledge layer, telemetry, and visible product-motion evidence, but contact sheets do not make a full end-to-end query/result legible.
execution_evidence: Demo is alive and video frame sheets show consistent store/documentation and result surfaces.
About text specifies two live stores, shared data, AbortController groups, and GA4 WebMCP telemetry.
Frame sheets are somewhat repetitive and weak on explicit before/after invocation evidence.
impact_rationale: Store owners and shoppers have a concrete need for expert product and policy guidance that generic catalog tools omit; the solution directly addresses that gap.
impact_evidence: Two named real stores and concrete queries such as plantar-fasciitis tape, kids sizing, and duties/shipping.
Knowledge expansion from 7 to 77 and 0 to 45 answers is described.
Human and agent doors are intended to stay synchronized.
creativity_rationale: The concept identifies a specific limitation of standardized Shopify agent tools and pursues a memorable dual-door merchant-expertise model.
creativity_evidence: Domain tools plus a knowledge playbook is a focused answer to the 'everything a human clerk knows' gap.
Same underlying data powers a human concierge and visitor agent surface.
usability_note: Read-only, structured schemas and visible results support trust; evidence does not show enough detail to assess all flows.
red_flags: Frame sheets do not clearly expose tool names, arguments, or a complete invocation trace.
standouts: Strong domain-specific delta beyond generic Shopify tools.
Shared knowledge layer and human/agent parity.
advance_reason: High-leverage, concrete WebMCP extension with a credible live-store use case and substantial implementation evidence.

one_line: Agents build and animate architecture diagrams on a shared canvas.

leverage_rationale: The structured visual grammar and shared live canvas make agent-authored diagrams practical and reversible in a way generic UI driving cannot match reliably.
leverage_evidence: Eight WebMCP tools operate directly on the live React Flow canvas.
About text describes ~100-element visual grammar, auto-layout, motion defaults, and one undoable Cmd+Z batch per agent edit.
Frame sheets visibly show an editor canvas with changing diagram states.
execution_rationale: The architecture, animation editor, local storage, export, and fallback behavior form a coherent product; the contact sheets show the editor but not every claimed motion/export step.
execution_evidence: Alive demo, public repo, and three frame sheets of a consistent diagram-editor UI.
Description specifies Next.js/React Flow/GSAP implementation and graceful non-WebMCP rendering.
Visual progression is plausible but detailed transitions are hard to read at contact-sheet scale.
impact_rationale: Developers and teams have a real need to understand fast AI-generated code changes and communicate architecture/process impact; animated diagrams directly address that pain.
impact_evidence: Clear audience/problem pairing: AI code changes are fast while architectural impact is hard to see.
Supports architecture, sequence, BPMN, and cloud-icon grammars.
Human review/refinement is built into the workflow.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-generated living diagrams, animation, visual grammar, and reversible human co-editing is a notably original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Turns code-change understanding into an agent-built animated visual artifact.
Shared canvas and incremental reversible edits are pursued deeply rather than adding a chat wrapper.
usability_note: Undoable batches, local-first storage, and ordinary-editor fallback are strong usability choices; frame text is too small for finer assessment.
red_flags: Contact sheets do not clearly show readable tool-call logs or a complete narrated end state.
standouts: WebMCP is central to the canvas grammar, not a bolt-on.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and creativity with a coherent, visibly implemented editor.

leverage_rationale: Agents operate on exact planner actions and shared state, with live visual feedback; this is more reliable than manually driving a calendar, though the underlying operations remain familiar.

leverage_rationale: Structured evidence and evaluation-boundary tools improve auditability and prevent an agent from silently rewriting forecasts; general browser driving would be less reliable for provenance-sensitive work.
leverage_evidence: Description emphasizes shared audit surface, site tools, protocol/provenance, cutoff rules, and integrity evidence.

standouts: Strong evaluation honesty and provenance design.

leverage_evidence: Nine consistency checks and five findings are described.

execution_rationale: The workflow is unusually specific and safety-conscious, with visible document-review UI and a coherent staged-approval model; contact sheets do not expose every check result clearly.

impact_rationale: Exporters, logistics teams, and reviewers face real costly errors and permission boundaries; the product helps detect and prepare fixes without unsafe autonomous edits.
impact_evidence: Specific five-document export pack and ownership distinctions.

Side-by-side evidence supports reviewer decision making.
creativity_rationale: The permission-aware correction workflow is a strong, original interaction model for agent assistance in document operations.
creativity_evidence: Agent can prepare but not apply/send changes outside its authority.

standouts: Concrete staged correction and document-lock semantics.

one_line: A catalog and installer for tested WebMCP tools on sites that lack them.
what_it_does: Publishes tested hostname-specific tools, installs them into real page WebMCP surfaces through an extension, runs them against live pages, and records results and touched elements.
leverage_rationale: It expands WebMCP from site-owner adoption to a tested, constrained tool marketplace for the rest of the web; fixed operations, declarations, route handling, and recorded execution are not comparable to ad hoc UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Extension installs catalog tools into the page's real WebMCP surface after user consent.
Tools use a fixed set of nine operations and cannot reach undeclared network/storage targets.
Every tool runs against the real page before publishing and records result and touched surface.
Frame sheets show a marketplace/social-catalog-like interface, though detailed invocation text is not legible.
execution_rationale: The submission describes a substantial end-to-end catalog, extension, interpreter, route-change handling, and proof workflow; frame sheets show a coherent interface but not the full installation sequence clearly.
execution_evidence: Alive demo, public repo, three video frame sheets.
Detailed handling of SPA route changes and page-load reinstalls.
Frames show consistent catalog/content surfaces but are repetitive and small.
impact_rationale: Users and site owners benefit from making useful sites agent-operable before native adoption; the catalog also creates feedback and proof for sites to ship tools themselves.
impact_evidence: Directly addresses the gap between WebMCP-enabled sites and the rest of the web.
One-click installation, public catalog, and tested-before-publishing workflow.
The proposal preserves user consent and constrained execution.
creativity_rationale: A personal marketplace and safe installer for retrofitting WebMCP onto non-adopting sites is a highly original, ambitious protocol-level concept.
creativity_evidence: Reframes WebMCP adoption as a catalog/distribution problem.

usability_note: Consent, preview of touched surfaces, and one-click install are strong; extension setup and SPA edge cases may add complexity.
red_flags: Contact sheets do not make a complete install-and-call trace legible.

standouts: Most transformative WebMCP concept in the packet.

Frames show consistent audio-tool UI and processing/control states.
